name: Sisera
title: Canaanite military commander
summary: Sisera was the military commander of Jabin, the Canaanite king of Hazor. He oppressed the Israelites for twenty years with his nine hundred iron chariots but was defeated by Barak and Deborah. He was ultimately killed by Jael, who drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept.

keyEvents.title: Oppression of Israel
keyEvents.description: Sisera, the commander of King Jabin of Hazor, oppressed the Israelites for twenty years with his nine hundred iron chariots.

keyEvents.title: Deborah's prophecy about Sisera's downfall
keyEvents.description: The prophetess Deborah told Barak that the Lord would deliver Sisera into his hands, but that the honor of victory would belong to a woman.

keyEvents.title: Defeat at the Kishon River
keyEvents.description: The Lord threw Sisera and his entire army into confusion before Barak. Sisera's forces were completely defeated at the Kishon River.

keyEvents.title: Sisera flees on foot
keyEvents.description: After the defeat, Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite.

keyEvents.title: Killed by Jael
keyEvents.description: Jael welcomed Sisera into her tent, gave him milk to drink, and covered him. While he slept, she drove a tent peg through his temple and killed him.

keyEvents.title: The victory celebrated in Deborah's song
keyEvents.description: Deborah and Barak sang a hymn of praise to the Lord, celebrating Sisera's defeat and Jael's deed as God's victory over Israel's enemies.
